title: Fallout: A Post Nuclear Role Playing Game
designer: Tim Cain, Leonard Boyarsky, Christopher Taylor, Jason Anderson
shortDescription: Interplay's grim, darkly comedic post-nuclear RPG that established the SPECIAL character system and retro-futuristic Wasteland lore.
historicalSignificance: Pioneered morally complex, open-ended quest design in Western RPGs where diplomacy, combat, stealth, and scientific intelligence were equally viable paths, backed by the iconic SPECIAL attribute system and 1950s retro-futuristic atompunk aesthetic.

editorialContent.overview: Created by a passionate division within Interplay led by Tim Cain, Leonard Boyarsky, and Jason Anderson, Fallout was released in October 1997 as the spiritual successor to 1988's Wasteland. Set in a desolate 22nd-century Southern California following a 2077 nuclear holocaust, the game cast players as the Vault Dweller, tasked with venturing into the radiated unknown to recover a replacement water chip for Vault 13.
editorialContent.gameplay: Built upon the SPECIAL system (Strength, Perception, Endurance, Charisma, Intelligence, Agility, Luck), character creation directly shapes dialogue trees, problem-solving, and survival odds. Combat operates on a turn-based Action Point system featuring targeted anatomical shots, accompanied by Mark Morgan's eerie ambient industrial soundscapes.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Integrated an intricate karma and reputation tracking matrix across disparate settlements (Shady Sands, Junktown, The Hub, Necropolis), producing non-linear narrative outcomes and distinct ending slides for every society encountered.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Fallout redefined Western computer role-playing, spawning an iconic entertainment empire encompassing major sequels, tabletop games, and a critically acclaimed television series, while popularizing Vault Boy and retro-futuristic Americana.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved through community patch projects (Fallout Fixt) and modern digital archives on GOG and Steam.

verifiedFactualData.sales: Over 600,000 copies worldwide in initial retail run
awards: Computer Gaming World RPG of the Year 1997

technicalSpecs.soundChip: DirectSound / AWE32 with Mark Morgan dark ambient soundtrack
